disposition_reason: The registered core findings and bounded implementation estimate biological associations and intervention effects. The paper provides no ordered held-out performance endpoint for these findings. Stronger association, larger plasticity or smaller p value cannot mean surpassing the paper; a new cross-mouse prediction study would be a separate extension.

source_paper.title: Distinct synaptic plasticity rules operate across dendritic compartments in vivo during learning

evidence.supports: The selected endpoints are pooled associations between coactivity and subsequent structural spine changes, supporting compartment-specific plasticity claims rather than held-out model performance.

evidence.locator: Record title, description and Repo_data_code.zip metadata
evidence.supports: Author release provides data/code for Wright et al.; the current record describes updated documentation. Metadata does not resolve historical release-to-caption discrepancies.

evidence.locator: Four endpoints and limits of the released_source_four_pooled_pearson_v1 component
evidence.supports: Historical score measures reconstruction of four released-source correlations, moments and support counts. It explicitly does not reward larger correlations or smaller p values.

target.description: Original scientific target is the relationship of local synaptic coactivity and dendrite-coincident activity to subsequent spine structural plasticity in apical versus basal dendrites, including compartment-specific Kir manipulations; the bounded legacy component reconstructs four pooled correlations.

dataset.description: Wright et al. processed data/code archive at Zenodo 15047046; equivalence of the currently selected release to manuscript-linked release and detailed source-row provenance remains unresolved.

cohort.description: Figures 2–3 early-training population: apical 375 classified spines in 19 dendrites/10 mice and basal 366 spines in 17 dendrites/12 mice. These nested counts are biological samples, not independently held-out prediction cases.

split.description: The selected paper panels report associations across the observed early-training population, not a training/validation/test prediction split. Creating a held-out-mouse split would define a new extension.

inputs.description: Observed local coactivity, dendrite-coincident activity and baseline/follow-up structural spine measurements. The observed structural outcome enters the association calculation and cannot be a candidate predictor in a new forecasting task.

preprocessing.description: Local-neighbor coactivity, compartment inclusion and structural-change definitions are described in the source, but full supplementary-method and release-version equivalence for the processed feature calculations is not resolved by this review.

metric.description: Pearson correlation and inferential comparisons describe the biological association. There is no defensible direction in which altering a true correlation, a plasticity effect, or its p value constitutes better task performance.

aggregation.description: Paper panels pool spine observations and report compartment-specific summaries; spines are nested in dendrites and mice. This is an association estimand, not an aggregate model-accuracy ranking.

comparison.primary_metric: No ordered performance metric for the registered compartment-plasticity association task

published_baseline.description: Published association estimates or exact re-computation are calibration targets, not an accuracy baseline that should be exceeded.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Published association estimates or exact re-computation are calibration targets, not an accuracy baseline that should be exceeded.

minimum_effect.rationale: No ordered performance endpoint exists for the selected biological association task.

uncertainty.method: No paper-win uncertainty test is defined for this ineligible objective.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Mouse, with dendrite and spine nesting for any separately designed biological analysis.
uncertainty.rationale: Uncertainty about a biological effect is not evidence that an algorithm surpasses that effect.

paper_win_requires: No paper win is admissible for the current descriptive association task.

A separately registered predictive replacement must name an original source-paper prediction target, fixed inputs, split, score and author baseline; a newly invented cross-mouse prediction task cannot inherit this paper-win identity.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison is asserted; the source-paper result and any later author rerun remain separate comparators.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive for same-task improvement. Preserve the original reconstruction and scientific interpretation as calibration work.
episode.candidate_freeze: No candidate may enter a paper-win evaluation under this ineligible contract.
episode.final_evaluation: Historical reconstruction remains scoreable but cannot emit a same-task paper win.
episode.baseline_policy: Keep published source score, reproduced author baseline, and any independently source-verified current SOTA separate. Reproduction is calibration only.

blocking_issues: No ordered source-paper performance endpoint for the registered correlation/intervention findings.
Historical release-to-manuscript correspondence and caption-statistic discrepancies remain unresolved; these do not create an improvement target.

legacy.notes: Preserve pooled-associations, matched-paper-packets, rep012-portable and registered-runtime unchanged. Their numerical/support scores calibrate source reconstruction and do not establish improvement, independent biological inference or whole-paper performance.
